paper.title: A Lipschitz Bandits Approach for Continuous Hyperparameter Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Pure Exploration Lipschitz Bandits with Batched Feedback
unmapped: Non-stochastic (hyperparameter-optimisation) model: assigning budget n to arm x returns a deterministic loss l(x,n) converging to a limit loss mu(x) with |l(x,n)-mu(x)| <= n^(-1/beta) (Assumption 1); the learner chooses the budget per pull and the total budget is T
Arm space ([0,1]^d, ||.||_inf); limit loss mu is L-Lipschitz
Learner uses the decay exponent beta of Assumption 1 (not the smoothness beta of the vocabulary)
Bounds depend on the zooming dimension d_z; the ACE sequence variant also needs d_z
settings.definition_quote: For any $x\in\mathcal{X}$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}_+$, the error sequence $\{\ell(x,n)\}_{n=1}^\infty$ is bounded by $|\ell(x,n)-\mu(x)|\leq n^{-\frac{1}{\beta}}$ ... The limiting loss $\mu(x)$ is $L$-Lipschitz with respect to the metric on $\mathcal{X}$

algorithms.name: BLiE (Batched Lipschitz Exploration), doubling edge-length sequence

source.label: thm:blin-upper
source.quote: If Assumption \ref{ass:hoeffding} and \ref{ass:lip} are satisfied, then output arm $\widetilde{x}^*$ of BLiE algorithm with total budget $T$, edge-length sequence $r_m=2^{-m}$, $\alpha=2L+2$ and $\beta$ satisfies $\Delta_{\widetilde{x}^*}\leq c\cdot T^{-\frac{1}{d_z+\beta}}$, where $d_z$ is the zooming dimension and $c$ is a constant. In addition, BLiE needs no more than $\frac{1}{d_z+\beta}\log T$ batches to achieve this simple regret.

results.notes: Losses are deterministic so the bound holds surely; c = (8L+8)c_0 depends on L, C_z, d_z, beta. Recorded as O.

source.label: thm:blin-upper
source.quote: In addition, BLiE needs no more than $\frac{1}{d_z+\beta}\log T$ batches to achieve this simple regret.

results.notes: Number of batches (communication rounds). The proof actually gives (1/(d_z+beta))log T - log c_0.

source.label: thm:ace
source.quote: If Assumption \ref{ass:hoeffding} and \ref{ass:lip} are satisfied, then output arm $\widetilde{x}^*$ of BLiE algorithm with total budget $T$, ACE Sequence $\{r_m\}$, $\alpha=2L+2$ and $\beta$ satisfies \[\Delta_{\widetilde{x}^*}\leq c\cdot T^{-\frac{1}{d_z+\beta}},\] where $d_z$ is the zooming dimension and $c$ is a constant. In addition, BLiE needs $\mathcal{O}(\log\log T)$ batches to achieve this simple regret.

results.notes: ACE sequence uses d, d_z, T.

source.label: thm:ace
source.quote: In addition, BLiE needs $\mathcal{O}(\log\log T)$ batches to achieve this simple regret.

results.notes: Number of batches. Proof: at most 2 log log T / log((d+beta)/(d+1-d_z)) + 1.

conditions: Holds for the uniform search strategy (Algorithm 3) with any grid length r
hard instance has zooming dimension d_z = 0, L = 1

source.label: thm:lower-us
source.quote: For any total budget $T$, dimension $d$ and grid length $r$, there exists an instance with $d_z=0$ such that the uniform search strategy returns an arm $\widetilde{x}^*$ with optimal gap $\E\Delta_{\widetilde{x}^*}\geq \frac{1}{2}T^{-\frac{1}{d+\beta}}$.

results.notes: Lower bound only for uniform search, not all algorithms.

conditions: Holds for random-search-based algorithms (sample N <= T arms uniformly, output one of them), e.g. Hyperband
for any given d, d_z, N

source.label: thm:lower-hb
source.quote: For any total budget $T$, dimension $d$, zooming dimension $d_z$ and number of selected arms $N$, there exists an instance such that any random-search-based algorithm returns an arm $\widetilde{x}^*$ with optimal gap $\E\Delta_{\widetilde{x}^*}\geq c\cdot T^{-\frac{1}{d-d_z}}$, where $c$ is a constant.
